newsitem.title: singapore: Asian dollar deposits quietly steady ahead of GDP.
newsitem.headline: Asian dollar deposits quietly steady ahead of GDP.

text.p: Asian dollar deposit rates were quietly steady in moderate trade, dealers said on Friday.

Most traders were sidelined ahead of tonight's release of the U.S. first-quarter gross domestic product (GDP), April new home sales, May Chicago purchasing managers index (PMI) and the May University of Michigan consumer sentiment index, they said.
U.S. first-quarter gross domestic product is forecast to show an increase of 6.0 percent compared with a 5.6 percent gain reported in the previous quarter.
New homes sales for April are expected to be around 800,000 units, lower than 813,000 units in March.
The May Chicago PMI is expected to be around 56.8 percent against April's 57.2 percent.
The May University of Michigan index is expected to be around 104.0 from its previous month's 101.4.
"The market has been quiet for the past three months or so. There was not much change as most people are concentrating on regional currency and not on U.S. dollars," a local dealer said.
In day-to-day rates, weekend rose 1/8 percentage point to 5-3/4 5-1/8 percent and Monday/Tuesday rose 1/16 point to 5-11/16 5-9/16 percent.
Week-fixed were unchanged from Thursday's 5-11/16 5-9/16 percent.

Among period rates, one month was unchanged from Thursday's 5-11/16 5-9/16 percent, three months unchanged at 5-13/16 5-11/16, nine months unchanged at 6-1/8 6 and twelve months unchanged at 6-1/4 6-1/8 percent.
